_doc: Degrees, counter-clockwise, that make_outputs.py adds to a footprint's KiCad orientation to get the CPL's Rotation, per LCSC part. JLCPCB places each part with its own model, drawn at an orientation of its own that a CPL angle is measured from (easy-stick 14.18); the table is what the JLCPCB placement preview showed on 2026-11-11 (issue #6): with the KiCad angle alone the model's pin 1 / polarity mark sat 90 or 180 degrees from the board's pad 1. A part not listed has none (its model matched, or it is symmetrical: R, C, FB1, D5/D6; the LEDs D10-D13 matched: the viewer's + mark, the anode, sat on the board's pad 2 at the KiCad angle, and a +180 first tried for them put it on pad 1). The table is keyed by LCSC number, not by package: the model belongs to the part. check_outputs.py reads this file too; it fails an entry no BOM line uses. Each entry is confirmed only by the preview after the corrected CPL was uploaded (JLCPCB_REVIEW.md in the release candidate).

C5137013.seen: model pin 1 on the bottom row's left end; the board's pin 1 is the top of the left column

C97521.seen: model leads on top and bottom, pin 1 bottom-left; the board's pads are in left and right columns, pin 1 top-left

C7433.seen: model leads on left and right, pin 1 bottom-right; the board's pads are in top and bottom rows, pin 1 bottom-left

C15127.seen: model pin 1 diagonally opposite the board's pin 1

C8545.seen: model's two leads on the side where the board has one pad

C6186.seen: model pin 1 at the right-hand end, the board's at the left (three-lead side)
